title: The Farmer and His Sons
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Farmer, being at death's door, and desiring to impart to his Sons a secret of much moment, called them round him and said, "My sons, I am shortly about to die; I would have you know, therefore, that in my vineyard there lies a hidden treasure. Dig, and you will find it." As soon as their father was dead, the Sons took spade and fork and turned up the soil of the vineyard over and over again, in their search for the treasure which they supposed to lie buried there. They found none, however: but the vines, after so thorough a digging, produced a crop such as had never before been seen.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Farmer call his Sons round him?
options: To divide his land among them
To ask them to fetch a doctor
To share with them a secret of much moment
To settle a quarrel between them

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Farmer tell his Sons lies in the vineyard?
options: A hidden treasure
A buried spring of water
An old family heirloom
A chest of ancient tools

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Farmer tell his Sons to do to find the treasure?
options: Sell the vineyard at once
Wait until spring
Ask a neighbor for help
Dig

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Sons use to search the vineyard?
options: Shovels and buckets
Spade and fork
Their bare hands
Plows pulled by oxen

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Sons find when they search for the treasure?
options: A small chest of coins
Nothing but empty soil and rocks
They found none
A note explaining their father's joke

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens to the vines after all the digging?
options: They produced a crop such as had never before been seen
They withered and died from the disturbed soil
They needed to be replanted the following year
They were sold along with the rest of the vineyard

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what was the Farmer's real purpose in speaking of a hidden treasure?
options: To test whether his Sons believed everything he said
To hide the location of real buried gold from strangers
To punish his Sons for being lazy in the past
To make sure his Sons would thoroughly work and improve the vineyard's soil

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did the Sons actually benefit, even though there was no literal treasure?
options: They inherited more land than they expected
Their thorough digging made the vineyard far more productive than before
They discovered valuable tools buried nearby
They were praised by their neighbors for their effort

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "impart" mean in "desiring to impart to his Sons a secret"?
options: To hide or conceal something
To sell something for a price
To share or pass on information
To forget something over time

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Hard work itself can be the real treasure, even when the promised reward turns out to be untrue
Farmers should never leave secrets for their children to discover
Vineyards are more valuable than any buried treasure
Sons should never trust their father's dying words

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what condition is the Farmer in when he speaks to his Sons?
options: Recovering from a long illness
Preparing to leave on a journey
Celebrating a good harvest
Being at death's door

questions.prompt: According to the passage, when do the Sons begin searching for the treasure?
options: Many years after their father's death
As soon as their father was dead
While their father was still alive
Only after they ran out of money

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how thoroughly do the Sons dig up the vineyard?
options: Only in a few scattered spots
Just once, quickly
Over and over again
Only around the edges

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the Farmer have chosen not to simply tell his Sons to work the land harder?
options: A promise of treasure motivates the thorough effort that direct instruction might not have achieved
He genuinely did not know how to phrase the instruction clearly
He wanted to keep the real reason for digging a secret forever
He believed his Sons would refuse to work without a reward

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the phrase "so thorough a digging" suggest about the effort the Sons put in?
options: It was actually quite minimal and careless
It was done unwillingly and resentfully
It was completed in a single afternoon
It was far more extensive than ordinary farming would have required

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "moment" mean in "a secret of much moment"?
options: Speed
Importance
Danger
Mystery

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A father hides real gold in his vineyard for his sons to find
The sons refuse to believe their father's story and never dig at all
A father's tale of hidden treasure leads his sons to dig so thoroughly that the vineyard flourishes
The sons find a treasure chest exactly as their father described
